caption: JLD matches MOS on two selected pairs with similar PSNR. Each row shows a reference and two distortions, with shared warm local displacement fields over the distorted photographs. A has the higher recorded human score; the three marks indicate agreement or reversal of this ordering. TID2013 shows chromatic aberration versus local blocks; held-out KADID shows JPEG compression versus colour shift. Both baselines reverse both comparisons, although PSNR differs by less than 0.02 dB within each row. The footer identifies metric symbols and agreement colours. Examples maximise the human-score gap under the stated selection rule and do not estimate population accuracy. Maps share one scale and exclude the global output term; scalar decisions include it.
selection_rule: For each dataset, enumerate same-reference pairs of different distortion types with MOS(A)>MOS(B) and absolute PSNR difference below 0.02 dB. Require the macro-named metric to prefer A and both DISTS and LPIPS-VGG to prefer B. Choose maximum MOS gap, then minimum PSNR difference, then reference/A/B paths lexicographically. KADID uses only the held-out test split.
